relevant_findings: Bare drywall priming is as much a dust-management and surface-conditioning workflow as it is a coating step.
PVA drywall primer is a standard baseline for new drywall to equalize porosity and improve uniformity for subsequent finishes.
Spray + backroll improves penetration and uniformity in many cases, but adds labor and requires protection planning.
Drywall finish levels drive inspection and correction intensity prior to prime; higher levels typically require more defect sensitivity.
condition_drivers: Dust level and jobsite cleanliness (active construction increases contamination risk).
Drywall finishing quality (tool marks, joint banding, fastener pops, fuzzing).
Lighting conditions for inspection (critical at QL-5).
quality_differences: QL-3: Standard inspection and touch-up; prime as a functional sealer step.
QL-4: Additional inspection and correction rounds; more consistent backroll where specified.
QL-5: Strict inspection discipline and surface uniformity expectations (often paired with higher-build strategies).
failure_modes: Fuzzing/raised paper fibers when primer hits dusty or poorly sanded surfaces.
Banding/telegraphing at joints if surface is not uniformly sanded and inspected under proper lighting.
Overspray contamination if protection is insufficient in active construction environments.
Poor uniformity if primer is applied unevenly or without backroll when needed.
notes_for_materials_manager: Maintain at least two primer strategy systems: standard PVA and higher-build primer option.
Consumables should include masking, plastic, roller covers, filters/tips for spray, and cleanup materials.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Include explicit dust control tasks (vacuum/wipe) and a fuzzing mitigation path (light sand after prime if needed).
Model inspection rounds and patch rounds as quality-driven repeats.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Use SF units for walls and ceilings; application method multipliers may be needed (spray/backroll vs roll-only).
Active construction environment should factor up protection and cleanup time.
assumptions: Numeric rates are placeholders pending calibration.
uncertainties: Drywall finish level declaration may not match reality; inspection may reveal additional correction work.
Spray vs roll productivity varies strongly with masking/protection burden.
